# unifi Provider

The `badgerops/unifi` provider manages **declarative UniFi Network configuration** through Ubiquiti's official Integration API (API key auth).

Use it for networks, WiFi broadcasts, zone-based firewall policy, DNS policy, traffic matching lists, ACL rules, DHCP reservations, and port forwards. It is built for configuration state — not day-2 operations such as device adoption, client telemetry, or controller analytics.

-> **New here?** Start with the [Getting started](./guides/getting-started.md) guide. Coming from `paultyng/unifi` or `ubiquiti-community/unifi`? See [Compared to legacy UniFi providers](./guides/vs-legacy-providers.md).

## Who this is for

- Operators who want Terraform to own site configuration on current UniFi Network releases
- Controllers that expose the Integration API (local console or UniFi Site Manager cloud connector)
- Teams that prefer API-key auth over a local admin username/password against the private controller API

## Who this is not for

- Device adoption, firmware upgrades, client blocking, or live telemetry
- Controllers that only expose the older private admin API and have no Integration API / API keys
- Full feature parity with every UniFi UI control — the provider tracks the committed Integration OpenAPI snapshot, plus a few documented legacy-API exceptions

## Requirements

1. UniFi Network with the **Integration API** enabled and an **API key** created in the UniFi Network UI (Settings → Control Plane → Integrations; exact labels vary by version).
2. Set `api_url` to the **base** controller URL. The provider appends `/integration` when needed.
   - Local console example: `https://192.0.2.1` or `https://unifi.example.com`
   - Site Manager cloud connector example: `https://api.ui.com/v1/connector/consoles/<console-id>/network`
3. Compatible with the Integration API surface tracked by this provider (currently UniFi Network OpenAPI snapshot **10.6.106**). Newer controllers usually work; refresh notes land in the changelog when the snapshot advances.
4. For zone-based firewall resources, enable zone-based firewall in the UniFi Network UI first. See [Zone-based firewall](./guides/zone-based-firewall.md).

## Example Usage

Prefer a pessimistic constraint such as `version = "~> 0.5"` in real configurations so patch releases are picked up automatically. The pinned version in the snippet below tracks the docs for this release.

```terraform
# Configure the UniFi provider with an integration API endpoint and API key.
terraform {
  required_providers {
    unifi = {
      source  = "badgerops/unifi"
      version = "0.5.2"
    }
  }
}

provider "unifi" {
  api_url        = "https://unifi.example.com"
  api_key        = "replace-me"
  allow_insecure = false

  # Raise this when the controller reprovisions devices mid-apply and requests
  # time out. Defaults to 30 seconds.
  # request_timeout_seconds = 300
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) API key created in the UniFi Network integrations UI.
- `api_url` (String) Base URL for the UniFi Network API. The provider appends `/integration` when it is not already present.

### Optional

- `allow_insecure` (Boolean) Disable TLS certificate verification. Only use this against trusted development systems.
- `request_timeout_seconds` (Number) Timeout applied to each HTTP request to the controller, in seconds. Defaults to `30`. Raise it when the controller reprovisions devices mid-apply: a UniFi Network application can stop answering its API for minutes after a WiFi change, and the default leaves a plan or apply failing with `context deadline exceeded` partway through.
